original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Does one independent generating set of length 27 inside the P112 punctured frame code, whose span contains all seven weight-16 supports, make research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py return that eight-word set at batch size 20, with support hash ff8861dab18040c03d403a860773218df7c120d03770d701afb61b78c941e3d3?
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a measured speedup that keeps coverage. Priority revision 8 says faster output is equivalent coverage only after the sets are compared. Open PR #7034 shows that the published intersection-counter engine refuses the 36-generator P112 basis at every legal batch size, and its ordered 27-prefix misses four supports. Its second open question asks for another generating set of length at most 27 whose span contains all seven supports. This package names one such 27-tuple, censuses that span, and compares one batch-size-20 stream. It records no timing and leaves the selected conditional exponent unchanged.
bottleneck_link: Decoder and deletion certificates can reuse a faster iterator only when that iterator still returns every low-weight word of the code being certified. This comparison binds the opt-in intersection-counter engine to one admissible length-27 generating set inside the P112 punctured frame code. It does not change a supplier bill or the selected conditional exponent.
stop_rule: Stop after one explicit 27-tuple, one Gray-code census of its span, and one batch-size-20 call to the published engine. Do not raise the dimension guard, edit engine.py, time the call, or rerun the 36-dimensional bit-lane census.
evidence: The seven published supports are pairwise disjoint weight-16 codewords, so their span contains exactly eight words of weight at most 16. Appending kernel basis vectors 0 through 19 gives the pinned 27 integers, with generator-list SHA256 2d580566f960c80d3f0f6f76342e83a4bf9b650ee9697226e58d8cc15da7da98. Those vectors are independent codewords and every support is a generator. A binary-reflected Gray code visits all 134217728 span vectors; eight have weight at most 16, and they are zero plus the seven supports. At batch size 20 the published intersection-counter stream is those same eight words, with positive-word SHA256 ff8861dab18040c03d403a860773218df7c120d03770d701afb61b78c941e3d3. Length 28 raises dimension exceeds 27. Batch size 10 raises batch count exceeds 65536. A repeated generator is rejected. The ordered 27-prefix remains a different tuple and misses four supports.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: Does this same 27-tuple return the eight-word set at batch size 11?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Batch size changes the engine's lane split. Batch size 20 uses 20 lane generators and 128 high-offset batches. Batch size 11 is the smallest legal batch for 27 generators and uses 65536 high-offset batches.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun this comparison with batch_bits set to 11 and the same 27 integers, weight bound 16, and support hash.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package stops after batch size 20, so batch size 11 has not been compared. The published dimension guard stays 27.

open_questions.question: Does one other admissible 27-tuple inside this code, whose span contains the seven supports and which is not this extension by basis vectors 0 through 19, return the same stream at batch size 20?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This census covers one span. A different subspace could contain another word of weight at most 16, and the engine could then return a different set.
open_questions.first_step: Name one other independent 27-tuple of codewords that contains every published support and is not this coordinate extension, then compare one batch-size-20 stream with the same hash.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package records one tuple. The 36-dimensional bit-lane census is open PR #7007 and is not replayed here.
